report.source_text: Because the prevailing clinical features were fatigue and dyspnea during effort, with only mild pathological findings on chest CT scan, a neurological evaluation was requested at this time to rule out a neuromuscular condition. The consultant neurologist outlined slight hypophonia after sustained speech, slight diplopia, and ptosis in one eye during sustained upward gaze and slight weakness in proximal lower limb muscles (scored 4/5 in the Medical Research Council scale), with normal deep tendon reflexes.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old man with hypertension and smoking history presented March 26 with cough, sore throat, and fever. SARS-CoV-2 PCR was negative, chest X-ray showed mild interstitial pneumonia, and he was hospitalized for 3 days in a COVID-19 ward before discharge on March 29 afebrile without respiratory dysfunction. Approximately 4 weeks later, on April 24, he presented with fatigue and dyspnea during effort; neurological evaluation was requested. Examination revealed slight hypophonia after sustained speech, slight diplopia, ptosis in one eye during sustained upward gaze, and proximal lower limb weakness (4/5 MRC) with normal deep tendon reflexes—consistent with generalized MG. Serological testing was negative for AChR, MuSK, and RyR antibodies (seronegative MG). Repetitive nerve stimulation on April 24 demonstrated a 15% decrement in compound muscle action potential amplitude in the right nasalis muscle at 5 Hz stimulation of the facial nerve, confirming the diagnosis. Chest CT showed no thymic residual tissue, excluding thymoma.
